correctness.rationale: On each strict mean-threshold activation cell the Jacobian is diagonal masking after weighted centering. Every proper mask occurs. Tree cut-step decomposition is an isometric coordinate representation of the weighted variation seminorm, so the induced Jacobian norm is exactly its largest cut-column ratio. For a cut, two constant opposite signed plateaus bound internal edge contributions and the bridge edge; a checkerboard activation on each component simultaneously attains all terms. A nearby pair in that strict cell realizes the maximum exactly. At two vertices only singleton masks occur, giving the separately proved mass-fraction formula. Unweighted path and star consequences follow from arithmetic of edge cut sizes. The checker of the actual packaged file passed 90,600 exact activation-column comparisons, 2,513 pair inequalities, and 180 explicit saturating pairs. Finite checks support, but are not used as, the proof of the universal claim.

value.rationale: This exact attained theorem completely classifies the two-input weighted BV sensitivity of a natural global-centering/positive-threshold operator on every finite tree. It reveals sharp linear-in-order instability on paths despite separate one-input TV contraction, a bridge-balance invariant, and star-versus-path structural extrema. The arbitrary positive masses and edge weights are mathematically integral rather than an arbitrary finite slice. Cycles and other nonlinear threshold maps remain meaningful unproved extensions.
